findings.title: Violet / indigo gradient
findings.why: The purple-to-blue gradient is the most recognisable AI-product colour move.
findings.fix: Replace with one flat brand colour. If depth is needed, use a surface step and a 1 px line, not a gradient.

findings.title: Text below WCAG contrast
findings.why: Grey-on-tint and pale-on-white text fails readers and audits alike.
findings.fix: Darken the text (or lighten the surface) until body text reaches 4.5:1 and large text 3:1.

findings.title: Stock framework palette
findings.why: Untouched indigo/violet/slate swatches from popular utility palettes make unrelated products look alike.
findings.fix: Derive the palette from the brand: one accent chosen on purpose, neutrals tinted toward it.

findings.title: Emoji used as interface icons
findings.why: Emoji in headings, buttons and list items render differently per platform and signal a quick draft.
findings.fix: Use one consistent line-icon set (one size, one stroke width) or remove the glyph.

findings.title: Gradient-filled text
findings.why: Headings or numbers clipped to a colour ramp are a stock "AI landing" signature.
findings.fix: Set the text in one solid colour; emphasise with size, weight or position instead.

findings.title: Coloured glow shadow
findings.why: Large zero-offset shadows in a saturated colour fake "energy" and hurt legibility.
findings.fix: Use a neutral, low-alpha shadow with a real offset, or no shadow and a 1 px border.

findings.title: Stock fake names and data
findings.why: Acme, Globex, John Doe and "User 1" are the placeholder cast of generated demos.
findings.fix: Use plausible, specific sample entries, and label them as sample data.

findings.title: Coloured stripe down one side of a box
findings.why: A thick left border on a card, alert or quote is a common AI shortcut for emphasis.
findings.fix: Emphasise with a tinted surface, a heading or an icon. Do not use a one-sided accent border.

findings.title: Eyebrow label above the heading
findings.why: A small, spaced, uppercase tag above every heading is a template habit.
findings.fix: Delete it, or fold the information into the heading. Keep at most one, and only if it carries a fact.

findings.title: Card inside a card
findings.why: Boxes within boxes add borders and shadows but no information.
findings.fix: Keep one container. Group inside it with spacing, a divider or a heading.

findings.title: Row of big numbers with small labels
findings.why: A strip of three or four headline metrics without a comparison is the standard hero-metric template.
findings.fix: Show one number that matters most, with its comparison base and date; move the rest into a table or chart.

findings.title: Pulsing status dot
findings.why: A blinking "live" dot on a status that never changes pretends the product is alive.
findings.fix: Show status only when it comes from data, as text plus colour, without animation.

findings.title: Focus outline removed without a replacement
findings.why: Keyboard users cannot see where they are.
findings.fix: Add :focus-visible with a 2 px outline (or ring) in an accent colour; never leave outline: none alone.

findings.title: Padding and gaps ignore a 4 px rhythm
findings.why: Values like 13, 18 or 22 px show that spacing was typed, not chosen from a scale.
findings.fix: Pick a 4 px scale (4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64) and snap every padding and gap to the nearest step.

findings.title: Heavy weights carry the hierarchy
findings.why: Weights of 800 to 900, or bold on most text, flatten emphasis. Hierarchy should come from size and colour.
findings.fix: Use 400 and 500 (600 sparingly). Let size and tone do the ranking.

findings.title: Border, soft shadow and tint on every card
findings.why: Stacking a border, a diffuse shadow and a different fill on the same surface is three signals for one idea.
findings.fix: Pick one separator per surface: a border, or a tint, or (for floating layers only) a shadow.

findings.title: Several text elements under 13 px
findings.why: Three or more small text elements make a page tiring to read, especially on phones.
findings.fix: Raise captions and labels to at least 13 px (body 16 px).

findings.title: Accent colour spent on decoration
findings.why: When the accent paints rules, tags and ornaments, it no longer tells the reader what to press or what changed.
findings.fix: Keep the accent for actions, selection, focus, live state and the key data series. Decoration goes neutral.

findings.title: Reflex font family
findings.why: Inter, Poppins, Space Grotesk and a few others are what models pick without a reason.
findings.fix: Choose a family on purpose and write the reason in DESIGN.md. A system stack is better than an unexamined default.

findings.title: Heavy resting shadows
findings.why: Large dark shadows on elements at rest make the page look puffy and dated.
findings.fix: Keep shadows only on floating layers (menus, dialogs) and make them subtle: low alpha, small blur.

findings.title: Greeting as a page heading
findings.why: "Welcome back, Sam" names no context; the heading should say what this screen is.
findings.fix: Name the content ("This month's scans"), not the visitor.

findings.title: Cards lift or grow on hover
findings.why: translateY(-4px) and scale(1.05) on hover is a stock micro-interaction.
findings.fix: Change tone or border colour on hover, only inside @media (hover: hover).

findings.title: No prefers-reduced-motion handling
findings.why: People who ask the system for less motion still get all of it.
findings.fix: Add @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) that removes or shortens animations and transitions.

findings.title: transition: all
findings.why: Animating every property triggers layout work and surprising effects.
findings.fix: List the properties you mean (opacity, transform, background-color) with a duration and easing.

findings.title: No texture, pattern or tonal light anywhere
findings.why: Every surface is one flat fill. Good pages carry a material: grain, a faint pattern or watermark, a tonal light behind the product.
findings.fix: Add one material that suits the project: fine grain, a subtle pattern in one zone, a watermark, or a soft light behind the main visual. Keep it quiet (under 10% opacity).
